newsitem.title: USA: Astronauts board shuttle for U.S. launch.
newsitem.headline: Astronauts board shuttle for U.S. launch.

text.p: Six astronauts boarded the space shuttle Atlantis on Sunday for a predawn blastoff on a mission that will take them to Russia's Mir space station.
NASA officials said the countdown was ticking smoothly toward a 4:27 a.m. EST (0927 GMT) launch from Florida's Kennedy Space Centre.

The astronaut crew, led by mission commander Mike Baker, began taking their seats aboard the $2 billion spaceship at about 1 a.m. EST (0600 GMT). Joining Baker were copilot Brent Jett and mission specialists Jeff Wisoff, John Grunsfeld, Marsha Ivins and Jerry Linenger.
Atlantis was to drop off Linenger on Mir for a four-month stay and pick up John Blaha, who has been aboard the orbiting complex since September.
Linenger, a 41-year-old Navy captain and medical doctor, is to spend four months on Mir, performing more than 80 experiments. Atlantis is due to return to the station in May to bring him home.
Forecasters were predicting cool but fair weather for the night liftoff. They gave Atlantis a 70 percent chance of getting off the launch pad during its narrow seven-minute launch window.
NASA launch commentator Bruce Buckingham said the shuttle's fiery climb to orbit on a northly trajectory should be visible along much of the U.S. East Coast.
Atlantis is the first of eight launches planned in 1997. The year is due to end with the first shuttle mission to assemble the NASA-led international space station.
